# Overview

Healthcare associated infections (HAIs) are a major problem in United States hospital systems. HAIs is linked to many factors, such as the patient's age or stay at a hospital, as well as the the hospital's infrastructure (e.g. number of available beds at the hospital) and staffing. Knowing how these factors affect patients is key for hospital leaders and institutions to implement policies in slowing down HCIs and better patient care. 

The main research question of this analysis is how do both patient and hospital factors contribute to a patient's infection risk?

# Data Description and Processing

The dataset contains data collected from hospitals in the United States, with each row representing one hospital.

Variables in our dataset are:

InfctRsk (numeric): Average estimated probability of acquiring infection in hospital (percent)
Stay (numeric): average length of patient stay (days)
Age (numeric): average patient age (years)
Culture (numeric): Ratio of number of cultures performed to number of patients without signs or
symptoms of hospital-acquired infection, times 100.
Xray (numeric): Ratio of number of X-rays performed to number of patients without signs or symptoms of
pneumonia, times 100.
Beds (numeric): Average number of beds in hospital during study period.
MedSchool (factor): Hospital has an associated medical school: 1 =Yes, 2=No
Region (factor): Geographic region, where: 1 =NE, 2=NC, 3=S, 4=W 
Census (numeric): Average number of patients in hospital per day during study period.
Nurses (numeric): Average number of full-time equivalent registered and licensed practical nurses during
study period (number full-time plus one half the number part time).
Facilities (numeric): Percent of 35 potential facilities and services that are provided by the hospital.
